counter_quote.original: Digital Reporting Requirements will affect cross-border B2B transactions from 1 July 2030.

locator.section: VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA), opening timeline paragraph

correction: The adopted 2025 package sets 1 July 2030 for general cross-border B2B digital reporting. Genuine 2028 platform and single-registration measures have different scope. The original 2022 proposal used 2028, which may explain the outdated date without establishing intent.
effect: Weakens the claimed external timetable for immediate action.
limits: Early domestic reporting is permitted, and preparing infrastructure now may still be justified by fraud prevention and implementation lead time. The correction does not disprove the policy request or its longer implementation path; it only weakens the stated EU timetable premise.
materiality_explanation: Major editorial judgment: the erroneous EU deadline advances the relevant mandatory cross-border implementation horizon by at least two years and materially compresses the preparation period presented to the reader. Independent reasons for early national preparation remain.
context_checked: The full section on pages 2–3 explicitly links 2028 to mandatory intra-Community reporting and immediately calls for national infrastructure. Its intended near-real-time system and other functions, alongside an architecture extending to 2035, distinguish the general DRR argument from optional early domestic systems and the separate 2028 OSS/platform changes.
